chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: The Palmer Brothers and Cab's recordings
summary: McRae describes the Palmer Brothers vocal group and Cab's records "I'll Be Around" and "Minnie the Moocher".

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, I want to ask you about some things here. Who were the Palmer Brothers? How many of --
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
They was like three brothers. They sang -- you know like the Modernairfes? They sang better harmony than the Modernairfes. They were great.

You don't have a record on them? They had a thing -- We got a double album on Cab -- on whatchamacallern -- I'll bring it. It's called "I'll Be Around," and his wife played on the record. (Singing notes) Cab was singing, the Palmer Brothers is singing in the background.
Is this a double record on Columbia?

Yeah. And I'm doing all the saxophone work. And that's the thing we did in Chicago, I was telling you about when we were at the Panther Room in Chicago. We did that up. We recorded out there nobody knew. (inaudible). They had been playing (inaudible). Cab
